_comment: AS.7 + DU.2 - an assistant whose tools are the other assistants. It still has NO grant over anyone else's SUBJECT: it cannot browse, cannot read the news feed, cannot touch Ledger or LoopStar. Everything it reports is asked for. What DU.2 adds is the ability to produce its OWN output - the daily report it was asked for, and that report read aloud. Writing up what you were told is not reaching into someone else's subject; it is the job.
blurb: Asks the other assistants what matters today and gives you one list.
_whyNoAinewsGrant: Deliberate. The coordinator could read ainews directly in one call, and that is exactly why it must not: the Reading assistant is the one that knows which subjects the user follows and which they have asked it to drop. A coordinator reading the raw feed would produce a generic digest and quietly strip the personalisation the whole design exists for.
_whyPublishIsGranted: Granted but classed dangerous in portal/capabilities.json, so it stops for approval every time. audiocast.create ALREADY delivers the audio to the user's iPhone through CloudKit - publishing is only for a subscribable RSS feed, which puts a file on the open internet under their name. That is the user's call each morning, not the assistant's.
_whyALongerRelayTimeout: Measured 2026-09-17. The flat 120s relay timeout is structurally too short for this assistant: its turn CONTAINS relayed turns, and each of those is itself allowed 120s. Asked to run a Daily Update, it was still waiting on the first of three handoffs when its caller gave up - so it could never report success no matter how well it worked. A coordinator's budget has to exceed the sum of what it waits on. Capped at 600s by AssistantRelay.maxTurnTimeout so content cannot hang a caller indefinitely.
_whyPinnedToClaude: 2026-09-17. Left null, the resolver picked codex, which was out of credits until Sep 19 - and it could not have known, because backendAvailability() reads the content invocation mappings, not the health probe. So a coordinator run failed for a reason nothing in the selection path could see. Pinned to claude, which probes GREEN. Set back to null once backend selection consults health; this is a workaround for that gap, not a preference about which CLI is better.
